title: introduce-rampdown-cost-advisor-and-mini-batcher-coordinator
author: Jordan M. Park
description: Summary: Adds a tenant-aware Rampdown Cost Advisor and a Mini-Batcher Coordinator. The advisor continuously scores tenants against budget and latency SLOs and emits short-lived 'rampdown' recommendations (temporary batch size reductions, cache TTL tightening, and conservative quantization levels). The coordinator receives those recommendations and applies tenant-scoped microbatch templates in the serving runtime with safe fallbacks to avoid SLO violations. Motivation: We see recurring short bursts of cost pressure from a small set of tenants that cause either sustained cost overruns or brittle manual interventions. Existing autotuners gestalt around long-lived defaults; this change provides an automated, low-latency control loop that (a) targets short-timescale budget smoothing, (b) reduces human toil, and (c) integrates safe fallbacks to prevent latency regressions. Design: - Rampdown Cost Advisor: a lightweight streaming analyzer in redwood/optimize that computes a time-decayed budget score per tenant using recent token spend, error rates, and latency percentiles. Outputs JSON recommendations with TTL (30–300s) and an action vector: {batch_delta, cache_ttl_delta, quant_profile}. - Mini-Batcher Coordinator: runtime component in redwood/runtime/batcher which can apply microbatch templates atomically for a tenant; templates include batch_size, max_wait_ms, and KV prefetch hints. Coordinator also negotiates with the kernel selector to prefer conservative quant profiles when recommended; all changes attach a correlation id and revert automatically at TTL expiry. - Safety model: each recommendation is simulated against a local cost/latency estimator; changes that predict >10% P95 latency increase are rejected locally. We ship a safety whitelist for latency-sensitive tenants. Backwards compatibility: changes are additive and disabled unless tenant-level advisor is enabled by config. Migration: config flag 'optimize.rampdown.enabled' defaults to false; rollout plan below. Implementation notes: - New infra: lightweight in-memory sliding windows for per-tenant metrics (time-decayed counters) persisted to redis for short-term coordination. - New RPC: coordinator exposes a small gRPC method ApplyTenantTemplate(tenant, template, ttl) used by the advisor. - Observability: added metrics optimizer.rampdown.recommendations_total, coordinator.applied_templates_total, coordinator.reverts_total and tracer spans on ApplyTenantTemplate. Testing: unit tests for advisor scoring, e2e sim harness that replays sampled tenant traffic and verifies no more than 5% regression in tail latency for safety-whitelisted tenants. Perf: bench harness shows ~3.9% median cost reduction for bursty tenants in our staging replay dataset with <1% median latency impact. Checklist: - [x] Advisor scoring algorithm implemented - [x] Coordinator apply/revert logic - [x] Safety simulator and whitelist - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs and config flags - [x] Telemetry and dashboards - [x] Rollout + kill switch Commits (summary): - feat(optimize): add rampdown advisor scoring engine and TTL recommendations - feat(runtime): implement mini-batcher coordinator and template application API - perf(kernel): conservative quant profile negotiation path - infra(redis): short-term tenant state persistence and TTL reconciliation - test: add replay sim and safety regression checks - docs: add operations guide and troubleshooting notes Files changed (high level): redwood/optimize/rampdown_advisor.py (new), redwood/runtime/batcher/mini_batch_coordinator.py (new), redwood/runtime/batcher/template_store.py (modified), redwood/runtime/kernel/quant_selector.py (hook added), redwood/infra/redis/tenant_state.py (new small shim), redwood/ops/docs/rampdown-advisor.md (new), tests/optimize/test_rampdown_scoring.py, tests/runtime/test_coordinator_revert.py, ci/workflows/e2e-sim.yaml (added sim job). Review notes and design rationale included inline. Rollout plan: stage feature off by default; enable for 5% of tenants in staging for 48h with monitoring alerts on optimizer.rampdown.recommendations_total and coordinator.reverts_total. If indicators are stable, increase to 25% canary for 72h, then 100% gradual rollout. Rollback: toggle config false or empty safety whitelist to prevent any new recommendations; coordinator will revert outstanding templates when TTLs expire. Backout patch provided for kernel quant hook if necessary.

review_thread: Asha Patel (reviewer) on 2025-11-03: Overall nice work. Concern: how do we avoid continuous thrash if a tenant oscillates? Suggest adding exponential backoff on repeated recommendations.
Author (Jordan) on 2025-11-03: Added a cooldown counter and exponential backoff to the advisor; see rampdown_advisor.py cooldown_backoff() and unit tests.
Diego Ruiz (reviewer) on 2025-11-05: Please add smoke tests ensuring coordinator applies and reverts under TTL expiry even when Redis latency spikes.
release_notes: Introduce Rampdown Cost Advisor (tenant-scoped temporary cost-smoothing recommendations) and Mini-Batcher Coordinator (tenant microbatch templates + safe quant fallbacks). Config-gated and off by default. Adds telemetry and an ops runbook.
